predictions.title: Las estaciones de trabajo LLM locales adoptan la carga firmada de tres niveles por defecto para Q3 2026
predictions.body: (Del resumen en inglés de hoy) By Q3 2026 the Wednesday three-tier-mitigation adoption wave forces the local-LLM workstation training-and-serving stack cohort — Unsloth, vLLM, SGLang RadixArk, Hugging Face TGI, llama.cpp, MLX, Ollama, and Foundry Local — to ship the paired load-time signed-checkpoint plus runtime manifest-allowlist-validation plus workflow-state path-canonicalization mitigation as the documented default load path at the local workstation tier rather than as serving-tier-only or opt-in features. The Wednesday catalysts are concrete and mutually reinforcing across all three tier surfaces simultaneously: SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 and Hugging Face TGI v3.2.0 ship the signed-checkpoint loader as the documented default load path for new installs on the same Wednesday (becoming the second and third open-source serving stacks at the serving tier inside one week, with SGLang the first to default it); Unsloth ships the workflow-state path-canonicalization mitigation in its Wednesday changelog tied to the AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 disclosure and the v2 joint preprint, becoming the first local-LLM fine-tuning stack to ship the workflow-state mitigation alongside the signed-checkpoint primitive ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target now extended to cover all three tier surfaces; the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft Wednesday v2 joint preprint addendum extends the Tuesday runtime-verifier integration to the workflow-state tier with reference implementations in Python and Rust; the Yotta Labs canonical benchmark refresh holds the vLLM-SGLang RadixArk throughput gap at 9.1 percent (essentially flat from Tuesday's 9.4 percent) with both stacks gaining 3 to 4 percent absolute throughput; the Cloudflare Infire L40S advantage closes to 1.12x (vs 1.18x Tuesday) with parity projected at vLLM v0.11.4 on Monday May 18; and Stable Long-Context RL via Router-Aware Advantage Decomposition v6 (arxiv 2605.05844 v6) demonstrates pre-tested integration against all three serving-stack loaders simultaneously — the first three-stack training-and-serving end-to-end formal-verification chain at the local-LLM workstation tier. The structural force is that once two production-tier serving stacks default the signed-checkpoint loader on the same Wednesday a leading local-LLM fine-tuning stack ships the workflow-state mitigation, and the v2 runtime-verifier preprint plus the Wednesday Verifiable Workflow-State Path Canonicalization paper (arxiv 2605.06799) anchor the cohort with reference implementations in Python and Rust covering all nine CVE-pattern instances, the remaining workstation-tier maintainers cannot leave unsigned or unmitigated loading as the documented default while the cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema and the CISA federal-civilian operational-directive working draft treat signed-load posture as paired procurement-eligibility evidence. The most likely shape is the three-tier mitigation becoming the default load path in the next minor release of llama.cpp, MLX, Ollama, and Foundry Local by Q3 2026 with explicit unsigned-load opt-out flags for sandboxed test fixtures and reproduction harnesses; sovereign-cloud and on-prem FedRAMP-Moderate workstation deployments adopt the loader first because the twelve-jurisdiction Indo-Pacific cohort exposes signed-load posture as a tenant-policy field. Bear case is that one workstation-tier stack ships a sandbox-only mitigation or forks the loader contract; absent that, Q3 2026 lands three-tier signed-load mitigation as the documented default at the local-LLM workstation tier across the eight-stack cohort.

reasoning.so_that: (Del resumen en inglés de hoy) llama.cpp, MLX, Ollama, and Foundry Local ship the three-tier mitigation as default.
reasoning.landing: (Del resumen en inglés de hoy) By Q3 2026; eight-stack workstation cohort; sovereign-cloud tenants first.
reasoning.plain_language: Las herramientas de IA local pronto rechazarán cargar archivos de modelo a menos que pasen tres verificaciones firmadas.

predictions.summary: (Del resumen en inglés de hoy) SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 and Hugging Face TGI v3.2.0 default the signed-checkpoint loader Wednesday; Unsloth ships workflow-state path-canonicalization the same day. By Q3 2026 the three-tier signed-load mitigation is the default at the workstation tier.

predictions.title: La SEC Corp Fin publica un Staff Legal Bulletin para IPO de aceleradores de IA para Q2 2026
predictions.body: (Del resumen en inglés de hoy) By Q2 2026 the Wednesday SEC Division of Corporation Finance second sample comment letter on AI-services-revenue measurement basis paired with the topical comment on hyperscaler-anchor warrant-equity counterparty disclosure shape — landing the day after the Tuesday Tenstorrent confidential-submission acknowledgement formally opened the 30-60 day review window — combined with SambaNova Systems' Wednesday confidential-submission cover-letter draft for late-June filing with the bookrunner roster locked at five (J.P. Morgan, Citi, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo Securities, Barclays Capital) referencing the Tenstorrent confidential acknowledgement as the operative precedent, Groq's process moving forward into the 21-45 day window pending Saudi PIF contingent secondary closure (the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU now described as on track for late-Q2 2026), and the Mag-7 print-cycle preview cohort coordinated update lifting the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability to 78 percent citing the post-IPO Cerebras CBRS Wednesday consolidation plus the Wednesday Corp Fin second sample comment letter as material structural additions, force the SEC Corp Fin precedent set to compress from the previously-modeled Q3 2026 staff-guidance shape window into a Q2 2026 publication window. The forcing function is that when the Corp Fin staff ship two operative sample comment letters plus one topical comment template inside a 5-business-day cadence and reference both as the named precedent set in two active 30-60-day-window confidential reviews (Tenstorrent in formal review Wednesday; SambaNova on a confirmed late-June submission target with the cover-letter draft already citing Tenstorrent as precedent), the staff-published-guidance landing cadence shortens correspondingly — the precedent set is now too dense to manage through per-S-1 comment letters alone before the SambaNova S-1 enters the public-filing window. The most likely shape is a Corp Fin Staff Legal Bulletin (CF SLB) issued before the SambaNova confidential-submission acknowledgement, covering the same three precedent-set axes already operative in the working notes (AI-services-revenue measurement basis, single-counterparty concentration risk-factor disclosure, hyperscaler-anchor warrant-equity counterparty disclosure) plus a fresh fourth axis covering AI-accelerator-supply-chain risk-factor disclosure shape (entailing the Apple Cerebras $4B multi-year supply agreement plus the OVHcloud Hetzner UpCloud Telefonica Tenstorrent Galaxy rack European sovereign-cloud commitments as the cross-vendor reference). Sovereign-wealth-fund and hyperscaler counterparty disclosure adopt first because the Saudi PIF Groq discussion plus the Apple Cerebras supply agreement plus the Anthropic-Blackstone JV template each surface counterparty-disclosure questions the existing Cerebras CBRS S-1 exhibit only partially answers. Bear case is the SEC Corp Fin staff defers a published bundle in favor of continuing the per-S-1 comment-letter cadence citing the existing precedent set; absent that, Q2 2026 lands a standardized Corp Fin AI-accelerator IPO disclosure CF SLB release before SambaNova hits the confidential-submission window.

predictions.title: La orden ejecutiva FMRB se firma para julio 2026 con cláusula espejo de adquisición aliada
predictions.body: (Del resumen en inglés de hoy) By July 2026 the Frontier Model Review Board executive order — driven by the Wednesday seven-witness confirmed slate for the May 15 14:00 EDT S-407 classified threshold briefing (Locascio, ODNI cyber lead, NSA Cyber, MSTIC, CISA Director, FCC PSHSB Bureau Chief, DOE CESER Assistant Secretary), the now-fourteen-organization amicus coalition (ABA Cybersecurity Legal Task Force plus NAAG AI working group join Tuesday's twelve-organization cohort), the coordinated House Energy and Commerce plus Senate Cyber request bundle for the parallel 30-day House technical review window citing the State Farm reasoned-decision-record requirement plus the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window alignment, and the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat's Wednesday-afternoon procedural note describing the Indo-Pacific cohort as on track toward thirteen-jurisdiction formal mirror count by Q3 2026 — signs with an allied-procurement-mirror clause that requires US federal-civilian procurement to recognize the eleven-plus-jurisdiction cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema as evidence of frontier-model pre-release vetting equivalence, closing the US recognition gap as a unilateral US action rather than waiting for a separate bilateral agreement with each cohort jurisdiction. The trigger is the Wednesday convergence of three structurally complementary moves: the witness slate firms to seven with the DOE CESER addition giving the briefing energy-security plus cyber-security plus cyber-resilience plus telecommunications-resilience plus civil-society perspectives in one panel, eliminating the most plausible OSTP-side delay justification; the coordinated bicameral request bundle plus the fourteen-organization amicus coalition narrow focus to the structural requirements (reasoned-decision-record, parallel House technical review, allied reciprocity-attestation 120-day placement alignment) that operate as objective gating criteria rather than partisan political preferences; and the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat's procedural note publishes a citable Indo-Pacific thirteen-jurisdiction Q3 2026 mirror-count trajectory that the FMRB executive order can recognize as evidence of an operative allied-procurement-eligible reciprocity perimeter without prejudging any particular jurisdiction's status. The structural force is procurement-driven: when the US recognition gap has widened to a full twelve-jurisdiction perimeter plus Brazil's formal exploratory entry plus South Africa's first African exploratory observer, the FMRB executive order's economic value-add increasingly depends on its allied-procurement-mirror clause rather than on its US-mandatory schema variant; the bilateral-equivalence pathway is administratively unworkable inside an executive-order timeline. The landing shape: by July 2026 at least one signed executive order issues with an allied-procurement-mirror clause covering the eleven-plus-jurisdiction cohort, and at least one Department-of-Defense or General Services Administration follow-on directive operationalizes the mirror clause as a procurement-eligibility filter for AI-services vendors. Bear case is the executive order defers the mirror clause as a Phase 2 expansion and ships only the US-mandatory schema variant; absent that, July 2026 lands the FMRB EO with the allied-procurement-mirror clause as a paired delivery.
